content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline spec is drafted. Per our SDD workflow, **this is a gate** — I won't plan or write any code until you've reviewed and approved the spec.

## 📄 Specification ready for your review

- **Spec:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md`

### What the spec proposes (in plain terms)

A personal app to **save**, **browse/open**, and **organise** web bookmarks:

- **P1 (MVP):** Save a link (auto-grabbing its page title, falling back to the URL), and see/open your saved links.
- **P2:** Search, tag & filter, edit, and delete (with confirmation).
- **Guardrails:** URL validation, duplicate warnings, best-effort title capture that never blocks saving, graceful empty/no-results states.
- **Explicitly out of scope for v1:** non-web link types, sharing between people, and browser import/export.

The spec is deliberately free of tech choices (no framework/language/database) — those come at the plan gate.

### One decision I need from you before this is approvable

Everything else I filled in with reasonable defaults (documented in the Assumptions section). This one genuinely shapes the whole product, so I left it open rather than guessing:

## Question 1: How are bookmarks stored and who uses the app?

**Context**: FR-012 — "System MUST persist bookmarks so they remain available across app restarts."

**What we need to know**: Is this a single-user app storing data locally, or a multi-user app with accounts and cross-device sync?

| Option | Answer | Implications |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| A | **Single user, local storage** | Simplest. Data lives on one device, no login. Fast to build; no sync between devices. |
| B | **Single user, synced across devices** | One person, but bookmarks follow them across devices. Needs an account/login and hosted storage. |
| C | **Multi-user with accounts** | Multiple people, each with private collections. Needs accounts, auth, and hosted storage — largest scope. |
| Custom | Provide your own | e.g. "browser extension", "team-shared collection" — tell me and I'll adapt. |

**Your choice**: _(reply e.g. "A")_

Once you answer this and confirm you're happy with the rest of the spec, I'll move to the **plan** gate (`speckit-plan`).

Option **A** — single user, on my own device, no logins. It's just me keeping my own links. Good call leaving that open; A is what I want.

Before you treat the rest as approved, though, I went through it carefully and a few things don't quite match what I picture:

1. **When I save a link I already saved** — a warning isn't really what I want. I'd expect it to just take me to the one I already have so I can tweak it (fix the title, add a tag). Not two entries, and not a dead-end "already exists" message.

2. **What gets grabbed automatically** — you've got the title, but in a long list a title alone gets hard to scan. I'd expect it to also pull in the little site icon and a short blurb/description of the page, so each item is recognisable at a glance.

3. **Bringing in my existing bookmarks** — you've put import/export out of scope, and that one I'd push back on. I already have a pile of bookmarks in my browser; being able to bring those in (and get them back out) is honestly a big part of why I'd bother switching to this. I'd really like that in, not later.

4. **Searching** — when I search I'd want to find an exact phrase if I put it in quotes, and to be able to search *within* a tag (e.g. show me things tagged "recipes" that mention "chicken"). And it shouldn't care about capital letters.

5. **Sorting** — "newest first" is a fine default, but sometimes I'd want to flip it to alphabetical by title. I'd like to be able to choose.

6. **Getting things out of the way without losing them** — delete-forever is good to have, but a lot of the time I don't want it gone, I just want it off my main list without throwing it away. Some way to tuck a bookmark aside and still get it back later.

7. **"Read it later"** — I often save things I haven't read yet. I'd love to mark those and be able to look at just my unread pile.

Sort those out and I think we're close. Everything else in the spec reads right to me.

This is looking really close — you nailled all seven, thank you. A few smaller things jumped out now that I can see it all together:

1. **Typing tags** — when I'm adding a tag, I'd want it to suggest tags I've already used so I can pick one, rather than me retyping it. Otherwise I'll end up with "recipe" and "recipes" and "Recipe" as three different things by accident.

2. **Doing things in bulk** — this matters most right after an import. If I bring in a thousand bookmarks, I don't want to tag or tidy them one at a time. I'd like to select a bunch at once and do the same thing to all of them — tag them, archive them, mark them read, delete them.

3. **What actually comes in when I import** — your description mostly talks about title and address. But my browser bookmarks are sorted into folders, and I'd want those folders to come across as tags so my organisation isn't lost. And I'd want the original "date added" kept, not reset to today.

4. **Notes** — when I write a note on a bookmark I'd like a little formatting — a list, a link, some bold — and to see it laid out nicely when I read it back, not as one plain blob.

5. **Saving a search I use a lot** — once I'm searching and filtering by tag, I'd love to save a particular combination (say, "unread cooking articles") so I can jump back to it without setting it up each time. Only if it's not a big lift.

On your question: **P2 is fine for both import and export** — I don't need them in the very first version, I just wanted them genuinely on the list, which they now are.

Sort those and I'm happy to move ahead.

## 📐 Implementation plan ready for review

`specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md` — plus `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `quickstart.md`.

### The approach in plain terms

A **local app that runs on your own machine** — you launch it and open it in your browser at a `localhost` address. No accounts, no cloud, nothing exposed to the internet; all your bookmarks live in a single file on your device.

**Why it needs a small "engine" running locally rather than being pure webpage:** three of your own requirements can't work otherwise —
- grabbing a page's **title/icon/description** (browsers block reading other sites' pages directly),
- reading/writing your **import & export files**,
- keeping a fast, searchable store as the collection grows.

Under the hood: Python engine + SQLite file for storage, React for the interface, Markdown for your formatted notes. You wouldn't see any of that — just launch and use.

### ⚑ Two decisions I owe you — as promised

**1. Saved searches — my honest effort read:** **It's a small job. I recommend keeping it.** A saved search is just a name plus the filter settings the app already builds for live search — one little table, reusing filtering that already exists. Roughly half a day, fully isolated, and it's built last, so if anything ever slips it's the first thing to drop with zero knock-on. **My recommendation: keep it. Your call.**

**2. Export fidelity — the flag you asked for.** I checked what the universal browser bookmark file can actually carry:

| Your data | Survives a standard browser file? |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| Links, titles, **original dates**, icons | ✅ Yes |
| **Tags** | ⚠️ Partly — travel as **folders** (universal) plus a tags marker some browsers read; others see only the folders |
| **Formatted notes** | ⚠️ Lossy — kept as **plain text**; bold/lists/links flatten. Read/unread & archived can't be represented at all |

So the standard format **can't** fully carry your tags-and-notes wish on its own. My fix: **offer two export options** —
- **Standard `.html`** → drops into any browser (tags as folders), some fidelity lost;
- **Full backup `.json`** → **loses nothing** (tags, formatted notes, read/unread, archived, dates) and re-imports perfectly here.

Building both is cheap since they share the same work, so the plan assumes **both**. 

**I need your call on:** (a) saved searches — keep or drop? (b) export — both formats / HTML-only / JSON-only, and are you OK with tags-as-folders in the HTML one?

### Where we are
- ✅ speckit-specify → ✅ **speckit-plan (this gate)** → ⬜️ speckit-tasks → ⬜️ speckit-implement

Give me your two answers (and a thumbs-up on the overall approach) and I'll move to **speckit-tasks** — the task breakdown — which is still before any code gets written.

Both answers easy, and you read them the way I'd hoped:

**(a) Saved searches — keep it.** Half a day and first-to-drop if anything slips is a fine deal; I'd like to have it.

**(b) Export — do both formats.** And yes, tags-as-folders in the plain `.html` one is fine by me — I get that's just what browsers can hold. The important part is that the **full backup** loses nothing: that's exactly the "my stuff isn't trapped" safety net I was asking about, so having it keep my tags, notes, read/unread and archived state settles that completely. When I'm exporting I'd just want it clear which of the two I'm getting and what each keeps, so I don't hand someone the lossy one thinking it's the whole thing.

On the overall approach — thumbs up. The "runs quietly on my own machine, I just launch it and open it in my browser, nothing on the internet" picture is right for what this is, and the reasons you gave for needing a little engine make sense to me. I don't need to pick over the technical parts; that's your wheelhouse.

Go ahead to the task breakdown.

No post-implement hooks. The MVP is built, verified, and **running right now**. I stopped at T023 as you asked — Phase 5 onward is untouched.

## ✅ MVP ready to play with — open **http://localhost:8765**

It's live in this environment on an empty collection. Paste a URL, hit Save, watch it appear, click it to open.

### What works (save + browse/open)
- **Save a link** — with URL validation, and best-effort title/icon/description capture that never blocks saving (falls back to the address).
- **Re-save protection** — saving a URL you already have opens the existing one instead of duplicating (even if it differs only by a trailing slash).
- **Browse & open** — list with title, icon, description, address; click opens in a new tab; friendly empty state when nothing's saved.

### Proof it does what we agreed
| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Backend tests (save / fallback title / malformed reject / dedupe) | **4/4 pass** |
| Live API — new save `201`, re-save `200`, malformed `422`, list | **all correct** |
| Frontend builds & is served with assets | **yes** |
| Playwright E2E specs (save + browse) | **written**, but ⚠️ can't execute *in my sandbox* — no root to install Chromium's system libs. They'll run on your machine with `npx playwright install`. |

I'm flagging that E2E gap honestly rather than claiming a green I didn't get. The backend tests are real and passing, and I exercised the live server end-to-end.

**To relaunch later:** in `backend/`, `. .venv/bin/activate` then `uvicorn src.app:app --port 8765`, and open the URL. (Frontend is already built into `frontend/dist`.)

### This is your play-and-feedback gate

## ✅ Triage (US5) is in — **http://localhost:8765**

New **All / Read later / Archive** tabs up top.

### What you can do now
- **Read later** — new bookmarks start unread (bold title + a blue dot). "Mark read" clears the dot; the **Read later** tab shows just your unread pile, with a friendly "all caught up" when it's empty.
- **Archive** — "Archive" tucks a bookmark off your main list without deleting it; the **Archive** tab lists them and "Restore" brings them back unchanged. Archived items stay out of your main list and searches.
- Delete (permanent, confirmed) still sits alongside, so you've got both "tuck aside" and "really gone."

### Plus your import wrapper-folder fix
Import now **skips the browser's top-level container folders** ("Bookmarks Bar", "Favourites", "Bookmarks Menu", "Other/Mobile Bookmarks", etc.) — only your *meaningful* folders become tags, so links don't arrive wearing four or five noise tags. ### Where we are
✅ MVP → ✅ US3 → ✅ US4 → ✅ **US5 (this gate)** → ⬜️ US6 bulk actions → ⬜️ US7 saved searches.

Two stories left. Say go and I'll pick up **US6 (bulk actions)** — select many (or everything matching a filter) and tag/archive/mark/delete in one go, which is where taming that freshly-imported pile really pays off. Then US7 (saved searches) closes it out.

Good — this is the everyday-use stuff, and the tabs are the right place for it. All / Read later / Archive is exactly where my hand goes looking for them; no complaints on where things live. Archive tucking something aside and Restore bringing it back untouched feels safe, and having that clearly separate from delete-forever is reassuring. I re-imported my file and yes — the "Bookmarks Bar" / "Favourites" noise tags are gone, just my real folders now. That's much cleaner.

One thing did feel off when I actually used it, though: **everything I save lands in "Read later" automatically.** That's not quite how I picture it. To me, most links I save are just... saved — reference, things I've already read, stuff I'm stashing. "Read later" should be the *smaller* pile I deliberately flag because I mean to come back and read them. If every single save starts unread, then my "Read later" tab is just a copy of everything until I go around marking things read, which is backwards from how I'd use it — I'd be doing chores to *empty* it rather than choosing what goes in.

So I'd expect a freshly saved link to be normal/read by default, and "read later" to be something I mark on the ones I actually intend to read. Whatever's cleanest on your end to route that — it feels like a behaviour thing to me rather than a screen tweak, but I'll leave the how to you.

Sort that and I'm keen to move on — go ahead with bulk actions, that's the one that'll finally let me tame the big imported pile in one go.

## ✅ Bulk actions (US6) is in — **http://localhost:8765**

This is the one for taming a fresh import.

### What you can do now
- **Tick several bookmarks** — a dark action bar appears showing "N selected."
- **Act on all of them at once** — add a tag, archive, mark read, mark unread, or delete (delete asks to confirm once).
- **Select everything matching** — filter to, say, tag `old-work`, tick one, and the bar offers "**Select all N matching**." One click, then archive or delete the *entire* filtered set — no ticking 600 boxes. It sends the filter to the server, so it acts on the whole match, not just what's on screen.
- Selection clears automatically when you change view or filters, so you never act on a set you can't see.

### Plus your read-later default fix
Freshly saved **and imported** bookmarks now default to **read** (a plain saved link). "Read later" is the smaller pile you opt into with "Mark unread" — so it's a deliberate shortlist, not a copy of everything you have to grind down. I recorded that as a spec refinement to FR-017 (the spec had never pinned the default) so it stays truthful.
